sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Track Laying and Overhead Catenary Power for Metro Tram Networks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Singapore on the Promotion and Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Countering Money Laundering (revised, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised, effective 1 July 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (State Council Decree No. 734, effective 1 March 2021).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registrar in the home jurisdiction of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain an apostille from the designated Competent Authority of the source jurisdiction after notarisation if required; no consular legalization. Non-Hague Consular path: authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the source jurisdiction and then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are parallel, exclusive, and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or designated government corporate affairs agency in the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain an apostille from the relevant Competent Authority; do not submit to consular legalization. Non-Hague Consular path: obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by Chinese Embassy or Consulate legalization. These two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and cannot be sequentially combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorising incorporation of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign investing entity, with signature and corporate seal notarised by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarise the resolution, then obtain an apostille from the source jurisdiction Competent Authority. Non-Hague Consular path: notarise, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Corporate Documents of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company register or notary public in the home jurisdiction of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certify the copy as a true copy, then obtain an apostille from the designated Competent Authority. Non-Hague Consular path: certify the copy, authenticate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The two paths are parallel alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the foreign investing entity, signed by a bank officer with corporate bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarise the bank officer signature and bank seal, then obtain an apostille from the applicable Competent Authority. Non-Hague Consular path: notarise, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. For some Chinese banks a SWIFT or telex verification may supplement but not replace the authenticated letter for WFOE registration.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every ultimate beneficial owner, director, and senior manager against the PBOC Beneficial Owner Information System, SAMR nationwide shareholder database, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists covering ISIL/Da'esh and Taliban sanctions regimes, China's Ministry of Public Security terrorist list, and the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Customer due diligence must verify identity, legal status, source of wealth, and beneficial ownership, with enhanced due diligence for PEPs, their family members and close associates, and for persons connected with FATF-identified high-risk jurisdictions. All sanctions hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and filed with PBOC in accordance with suspicious transaction reporting rules. Negative media and political exposure risk assessments must be documented contemporaneously and retained for no less than five years after account closure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Online Registration and Confirmation Platform, accessible through the SAMR integrated government service portal at https://zwfw.samr.gov.cn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese company name must contain four elements in order: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and legal form reflected as 有限责任公司. The trade name must contain at least two Chinese characters; pinyin may appear only within a Chinese-character name and not as a standalone script. The registered Chinese name must be used consistently across the business license, seals, tax registration, and bank accounts. A foreign company name may be recorded as a supplementary item after the Chinese name, but the Chinese name carries legal effect. Phonetic transliteration into Chinese characters is required, and the chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing enterprise name.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects a pre-registered company name, the applicant must first request an online written explanation through the same SAMR portal within five working days. If rejection is maintained, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the next-higher market regulation authority within 60 days from the written notification, or file an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within six months. The appeal must include the original application number, the detailed reason for rejection, and any prior ministerial approval or supporting trademark evidence for a prohibited or sensitive token. The name reservation can be extended once for an additional 30 days before expiry by submitting an online extension request; after a rejection, two to three corrected name variants should be submitted immediately to preserve priority.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 13, 14, 23-31, 34-38, 47, 51, 59-63, 75, 82; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 17, 20-22; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, 2021), Articles 1-9, 12, 16-24; Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration Administration (SAMR Order, 2020).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration / Municipal Administrative Approval Bureau where the registered office is located, using the National Enterprise Registration Online Service and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (https://www.gsxt.gov.cn).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company, together with the approved Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's resolution, and the foreign investor's authenticated corporate existence certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a WFOE limited liability company under the current PRC Company Law. The shareholder may subscribe the full registered capital in the Articles of Association, and the capital contribution schedule must be completed within five years from the date of incorporation unless a special industry rule imposes a shorter or higher threshold. No blocked escrow account is statutorily mandated for formation; however, if the light rail EPC contract is funded through a government bond escrow or performance-guarantee mechanism, the project owner will require a separate escrow / performance-guarantee account which is contractual and not a corporate law formation condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (the Company). The undersigned directors, constituting the entire first board of directors of the Company, acting pursuant to the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association of the Company, do hereby adopt and record the following resolutions on this day of [DATE]. 1. Incorporation and Share Capital Subscription. The Board approves the form and content of the Articles of Association and all ancillary incorporation documents submitted to the Board, and authorises the legal representative designate to execute and file the Application for Establishment Registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation. The Board ratifies the subscription by the sole foreign shareholder of 100% of the registered capital of the Company in the amount of RMB [AMOUNT] set forth in the Articles of Association. Such subscription is accepted, and management is instructed to establish a capital contribution record and any project-specific escrow account required by a client or lender under the urban light rail transit EPC agreement. 2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorises and directs the Legal Representative, the Chief Financial Officer, and such other persons as the Board may designate to open, maintain, and operate the Company's basic deposit account, foreign exchange capital account, and such other bank accounts as may be required with a bank licensed to conduct foreign exchange business in China. Any two designated signatories shall act jointly for wire transfers and SWIFT payment instructions, and each bank mandate card must be approved in writing by the Board. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS] as the registered office and statutory domicile of the Company for service of process, tax registration, license filings, and corporate records. Management is directed to file the lease and property ownership documents with the registration authority and to post the business license sign at this address. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [NAME] as Legal Representative and Executive Director; [NAME] as General Manager; [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer; [NAME] as Chief Compliance Officer; and [NAME] as Manager of Construction Licensing and EHS Compliance. All appointees shall hold office at the pleasure of the Board and are granted full authority to execute documents and make declarations within their respective scopes. 5. Seals and Governance Instruments. The Board approves the engraving and use of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal and legal representative seal, and establishes a seal-use control policy requiring dual approval for contracts above [AMOUNT]. 6. Regulatory and Industrial License Approval. The Board directs management to apply without delay for the Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate, Construction Enterprise Safety Production License, Environmental Impact Assessment approval, fire protection design review, civil defense clearance, and all other permits required for track laying and overhead catenary power works under ISIC 4210. All corporate actions taken in reliance on these authorizations are ratified. 7. Effective Date. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption, and the Chairman of the Board is authorised to certify a conformed copy for submission to banks, government authorities, and project counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Negative List Clearance and Enterprise Name Pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a legal mapping of the proposed business scope, namely urban light rail transit track laying and overhead catenary power EPC under ISIC 4210 / NAICS 237990, against the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access commonly known as the Foreign Investment Negative List. Confirm that the proposed activity is not within a prohibited or restricted category requiring a sectoral foreign investment approval. Prepare one primary and two fallback company names, selecting CN_WFOE_LTD as the English name and an approved transliterated Chinese name. Submit the online enterprise name pre-approval application, upload the foreign shareholder's authenticated identity documents with Chinese translation, the agent's authorization letter, and a business scope explanation. Retain the Name Pre-approval Notice for use in the subsequent establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Name Pre-approval Application Form
Foreign shareholder Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent legal existence certificate
Apostille or consular legalization certificate and notarized Chinese translation
Authorization Letter appointing the contact person or registration agent
Business scope and industry classification description covering ISIC 4210 and NAICS 237990
Negative List compliance confirmation and any required sectoral pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected or suspended for similarity, refile with a more distinctive industry feature or obtain a written consent letter from the earlier name holder. If the negative list determination is queried, escalate the matter to the MOFCOM foreign investment information service for a written classification before resubmitting the name application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Authentication and Preparation of Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent notary office in the foreign investor's jurisdiction, Chinese Embassy/Consulate or Hague Apostille authority, and local licensed translator in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's written resolution, the first board resolution, the legal representative appointment letter, the supervisor appointment letter, director consent forms, and the capital contribution schedule. For documents executed outside China, notarize the foreign shareholder's incorporation certificate and board approval, affix an Apostille if the source country is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, or complete consular legalization in non-Convention states. Have all foreign-language documents translated into Chinese by a qualified translation agency with a translator's seal. Verify that the proposed registered office lease and property ownership certificate permit construction-engineering and EPC management use, and ensure that each signature date matches the registration timeline.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association of CN_WFOE_LTD
Sole shareholder's incorporation certificate and corporate power of attorney
Notarized and authenticated resolution of the sole shareholder
Apostille or consular legalization certificate
Sworn Chinese translation by a licensed translation company
Registered office lease agreement and property ownership certificate
Consent and identity documents of the legal representative, directors, supervisor and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If authentication is deemed deficient, obtain a supplementary notarization and apostille or contact the Chinese consulate for legalization assistance. If the registry rejects the Chinese translation, replace it with a translation bearing the seal of a PRC-registered translation service and resubmit within the prescribed correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration Filing with the Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration / SAMR integrated enterprise registration online system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the National Enterprise Registration Online Service and complete the application for establishment of a foreign-invested limited liability company. Enter the pre-approved name, registered address, legal representative, board members, supervisor, registered capital, contribution schedule, duration, and exact business scope concerning urban rail transit engineering and overhead catenary power works. Upload the Name Pre-approval Notice, authenticated foreign shareholder documents, Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's written decision, appointment letters, identity files, lease and title evidence, and the applicant's written undertaking of authenticity. Confirm that the integrated foreign investment information report is automatically transmitted through the SAMR-MOFCOM data exchange. The electronic Business License will be issued with a unified social credit code upon approval, which constitutes the statutory formation date.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company
Notification of Name Pre-approval
Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder
Written decision or shareholder's resolution of the sole foreign shareholder
Identity and qualification certificates of the legal representative and supervisor
Registered office lease agreement and property ownership documents
Authenticated foreign investor corporate documents and certified Chinese translation
Undertaking of authenticity signed by the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority issues a correction notice, file the necessary amendments online within fifteen days. If the application is rejected, cure the stated deficiency and resubmit. An unlawful refusal may be challenged by administrative reconsideration to SAMR or the local municipal government, and all submission time stamps and correspondence should be preserved as evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seals, Tax, Foreign Exchange, Social Insurance and Statistical Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving enterprise, State Taxation Administration local tax bureau, SAFE designated foreign exchange bank, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and local statistics authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after issuance of the Business License, engage a public security bureau authorized engraver to produce the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal and legal representative seal, and file the seal impressions in the public security record. Register the company with the local state tax bureau through the electronic tax platform, obtain the tax registration number, confirm the VAT classification for construction services and EPC contracts, and register the legal representative and financial officer. Open a basic deposit account and, if foreign capital will be injected, a foreign exchange capital account with a SAFE-designated bank, completing the Foreign Exchange Registration through the bank platform. Register the company and all employees for social insurance and housing fund, and complete the statistical declaration filing. All post-registration steps should be completed within thirty calendar days of the license date to avoid late-filing penalties.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copies
Unified social credit code certificate
Legal representative and financial officer identity documents
Seal record filing certificate from the authorized engraver
Registered office address proof and Articles of Association for bank and tax use
Foreign exchange registration forms if a capital account is required
Employment contract template and social insurance enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration deadline has been missed, make the delayed filing online immediately, pay any applicable minor administrative fine, and attach an explanation requesting mitigation for a first-time delay. For foreign exchange discrepancies, instruct the bank to file a supplementary SAFE report and correct the capital account settlement purpose statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Industrial Qualification, Environmental Assessment and Fire Safety Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD), provincial/municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, Ministry of Ecology and Environment / provincial Ecology and Environment Department, Fire and Rescue Department, and local Emergency Management Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing any urban light rail transit construction, track laying, or overhead catenary power installation, obtain the Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate for urban rail transit engineering professional contracting and, if in-house catenary and traction power works are performed, the railway electrical engineering specialized contracting qualification. Obtain the Construction Enterprise Safety Production License in parallel. File the project-level Environmental Impact Report with the competent ecology and environment authority and obtain the formal EIA approval document; apply for a pollutant discharge permit if any construction sewage or stormwater discharge point exists. Submit the fire protection design for review and, after completion, schedule the fire protection inspection for site offices, temporary structures, traction substations and catenary support facilities. Register the construction site with the local work safety administration and keep all special operation permits current.
required_dossiers: Business License and Articles of Association
Legal representative identity certificate and company seal
Technical personnel qualification certificates and registered professional certificates
Safety production responsibility system and emergency response plans
Environmental Impact Report and EIA approval decision
Fire protection design documents and completion inspection records
Construction site layout, structural load calculations and temporary works drawings
Work safety insurance certificates and safety fund payment vouchers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the qualification application is refused, file an administrative appeal to MOHURD within sixty days or supplement the missing registered technical personnel and resubmit. For EIA comments, revise the report and resubmit to the evaluation center; for fire safety, implement all rectification items set out in the correction notice and request a re-inspection before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD), provincial/municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Development Bureau, Ministry of Ecology and Environment and provincial Ecology and Environment Department, Fire and Rescue Department, and local Emergency Management Bureau
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Construction Enterprise Qualification Certificate for Urban Rail Transit Engineering Professional Contracting and Railway Electrical Engineering Specialized Contracting, together with the Construction Enterprise Safety Production License and Urban Rail Transit EPC Operating Permit / Work Safety Filing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China and the provincial Ecology and Environment Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Report (EIA Report) under the Classified Management List of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects. Urban rail transit line and traction power construction works are generally classified at the report level rather than the registration level, requiring formal review and written approval before construction; a simplified Environmental Registration Certificate is not sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All construction wastewater and oily water must be treated on site; if discharged to a municipal sewer, the discharge must comply with GB/T 31962-2015 (pH 6.5-9.5, COD <= 500 mg/L, BOD5 <= 300 mg/L, suspended solids <= 400 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen <= 45 mg/L). Air emissions from coating, welding and painting operations must comply with GB 16297-1996, including fugitive non-methane hydrocarbon boundary concentration <= 4.0 mg/m3 and particulate matter boundary concentration <= 1.0 mg/m3, plus any stricter local emission standards. Hazardous waste such as waste oils, paint residues, spent solvents, used batteries and oil-contaminated absorbents must be identified under the National Hazardous Waste Inventory, stored in facilities meeting GB 18597-2023, and transported only by licensed carriers with an electronic manifest. Construction site noise must not exceed GB 12523-2011 limits of 70 dB(A) Leq during daytime and 55 dB(A) Leq at night.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Protection Design Review and Completion Fire Protection Inspection certificates from the Fire and Rescue Department are required for site offices, temporary buildings, traction substations and catenary maintenance facilities. Structural load inspection and approval must be obtained for overhead catenary gantries, temporary bridges and heavy lifting platforms. The construction site must obtain a Work Safety Facility Design Review and Completion Acceptance under the Work Safety Law, file with the local Emergency Management Bureau, and register all special operations personnel such as electricians, welders, riggers and crane operators. Civil defense coordination with the local Civil Defense Office is required where underground light rail sections, station excavation or tunnel works exceed civil air defense thresholds, together with the relevant temporary construction clearance and special railway/tram interface permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China via the electronic tax portal of the provincial/municipal tax service bureau; foreign non-resident entities file initial registrations through the State Taxation Administration's online tax service platform (电子税务局, operated by the STA) after obtaining a taxpayer identifier through the State Administration for Market Regulation for the WFOE establishment process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company formed in China must first complete incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), obtaining a unified social credit code (USCC) that serves as the taxpayer identification number (TIN). Thereafter, the WFOE must complete tax registration at the competent in-charge tax authority within 30 days of obtaining the business license, file the taxpayer registration form, legal representative identity documentation, articles of association, business license copy, bank account information, and lease/ownership proof of registered address through the electronic tax bureau portal or in-person service hall. The STA issues a taxpayer identification number equal to the unified social credit code, activates the taxpayer status, assigns tax categories (VAT, corporate income tax, stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, etc.), and sets the filing frequency and tax administration district. For purely foreign non-resident entities without a Chinese establishment, a non-resident taxpayer identification number and withholding tax enrollment are obtained via the electronic tax bureau by filing a non-resident tax registration with the competent tax authority where the payer is located or where the real estate or income source is situated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity-level classification; China does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for limited liability companies. General anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and special tax adjustment mechanisms apply to controlled foreign corporations and hybrid mismatch arrangements under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, but no statutory pass-through election is available for a WFOE limited liability company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) administered under the People's Republic of China Interim Regulation on Value-Added Tax and the VAT Law adopted via the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, effective November 1, 2024, together with the Measures for the Administration of Collection of Consumption Tax, urban maintenance and construction tax and education surcharges as supplementary indirect taxes; for sales of goods, processing, repair and replacement services, and taxable services, but not a US-style sales and use tax or a full GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable sales threshold of RMB 5,000,000 for general VAT taxpayer status; small-scale taxpayers with annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000 and simplified collection rate of 3% (reduced statutory concessions may apply). Entities that do not meet the threshold may still voluntarily register as general VAT taxpayers if they meet the accounting and information requirements; mandatory general taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 unless the entity meets the simplified small-scale taxpayer conditions and does not apply for general status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the nationwide e-invoice system under the State Taxation Administration's fully digital electronic invoice (全面数字化的电子发票, also called 数电票) platform. Taxpayers must use the STA's official electronic invoice service platform to issue legally valid digital invoices; the platform performs real-time fiscal clearance, assigns unique invoice codes, and may require risk-based anti-fraud controls. General VAT taxpayers must use the special VAT invoice system for output VAT invoicing and input VAT credit certification through the VAT invoice comprehensive service platform (增值税发票综合服务平台). The e-invoice platform uses real-time data transmission, automatic revenue reconciliation, and digital tax control stamping; no separate physical offline invoice stamping is permitted except under transitional paper invoices which are being phased out. All invoice data must be reported to the STA electronic database, with mandatory API integration for enterprise resource planning systems or approved third-party fiscal service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to exported goods, cross-border taxable services, and certain offshore services rendered by Chinese residents to overseas recipients, under the VAT export tax rebate (exemption and credit) system. The statutory criteria require the goods to be physically shipped from a Chinese customs supervised area to a destination outside the customs territory of China according to a customs export declaration, with the sale made between a Chinese registered seller and an overseas buyer; the seller must receive payment in foreign currency or RMB settled through approved cross-border channels, and the goods must be actually exported within the prescribed time limits. For services, zero-rating applies to cross-border services that are consumed entirely outside China and satisfy the administrative announcement criteria on cross-border taxable services zero-rating and VAT exemption, including international transportation, research and development services, design services, software services, and other qualifying offshore services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) completed in the China International Trade Single Window and bearing the customs clearance release record
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export of the goods from China customs territory
Official export invoice or commercial invoice issued by the WFOE to the overseas customer

Foreign exchange receipts record (涉外收入申报单) or bank receipt voucher evidencing inbound remittance from the overseas buyer, and where applicable the receipt of export proceeds as filed through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
Letter of Credit or sales contract, if available, to corroborate the export transaction and payment terms
Customs clearance record of the goods, including the export goods after verification record and export rebate declaration list submitted via the export tax rebate filing system
Foreign exchange settlement and sale verification documents prescribed by SAFE to prove receipt of the export proceeds within the statutory time limit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The exporter must substantiate each zero-rated export transaction through the electronic export tax rebate system of the State Taxation Administration. If the foreign exchange proceeds are not received within the required time limit or the export is later found to have been falsely declared as exported, the tax authority will claw back the refunded VAT and charged interest, and impose penalty fines of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded amount under the Law on Administration of Tax Collection; moreover, failure to declare or mis-declaration of exports may lead to customs fines under the Customs Law, loss of tax rebate eligibility, blocking of future rebate filings, downgrading of the taxpayer credit rating, and criminal liability for fraudulent export rebate claims under the Criminal Law, including imprisonment and fines for the crime of fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the State Council of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a hybrid foreign exchange control regime in which the RMB is fully convertible for most current-account transactions, such as trade in goods and services, while capital-account transactions remain subject to registration, verification, and supervisory control by SAFE. For the proposed WFOE engaged in urban light rail transit EPC, inbound equity capital from abroad must be routed through a SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account opened at a licensed domestic commercial bank. Every conversion of those funds into RMB for project expenditure is scrutinized by the designated bank against the declared business scope and the underlying construction and EPC contracts. Convertibility is therefore asymmetric: export and trade proceeds can be settled freely after authenticity review, but cross-border outbound flows such as dividend remittances, shareholder loan repayments, and disinvestment proceeds require audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and board resolutions. Surplus capital cannot be diverted to non-business purposes or speculative financial investments. Profit remittances are permitted once tax and audit obligations are satisfied, but all transfers must occur through the formal banking channel. Offshore RMB clearing is permitted via the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) or the correspondent banking network, while physical RMB cash movement remains tightly regulated. This creates a bank-centric treasury architecture where capital account funds must be ring-fenced, conversion risk must be actively managed, and each disbursement must be supported by authentic trade or investment documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE trade-in-goods administration framework, there is no mandatory surrender requirement and no compulsory conversion ratio; export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in a domestic foreign exchange account. However, export earnings from goods trade must be repatriated to China through a designated bank within 90 days of the customs export declaration. If collection occurs later than 90 days, the enterprise must complete trade credit and receivable registration in the SAFE Trade Credit Reporting System. Any conversion of export proceeds into RMB requires authenticity documents such as the customs declaration, commercial invoice, contract, and proof of shipment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (SAFE-registered) and Basic Operational Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
Capital Account, CNY Basic Account, and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account and General RMB Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Offshore digital electronic money institutions and cross-border fintech payment platforms do not hold a commercial banking license in Mainland China and are not authorized by PBOC or SAFE to provide domestic CNY clearing, receive statutory capital contributions, issue RMB corporate accounts, or complete the SAFE foreign exchange capital registration for a WFOE. They cannot support capital verification for foreign direct investment or act as a clearing rail for government bond escrow. Their use is limited to non-statutory ancillary cross-border invoicing or outside-China treasury operations. The statutory treasury function for the WFOE must be maintained with a licensed Tier-1 domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBOC anti-money laundering rules, the statutory legal representative of a corporate entity opening a new bank account is generally required to appear physically in-branch for an interview at least once. For a WFOE, the statutory directors may alternatively delegate an authorized local manager who must appear in person with a notarized board resolution and a valid power of attorney. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted as a complete substitute for the first account opening interview. The bank also requires original corporate seals, the legal representative's notarized and apostilled identity documents, and SAFE registration confirmation before the capital account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained cross-border ownership chain and inconsistent ultimate beneficial ownership filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete group structure chart showing every intermediary entity up to the natural person shareholder, notarized and apostilled passports or national ID documents, corporate registration certificates and articles of association for each holding layer, an external UBO declaration, and a written explanation of the source of equity capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening hits on shareholders, directors, or project counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sanctions and PEP declarations, a third-party due diligence screening report covering UN, OFAC, EU, and Chinese sanctions lists, a detailed exposure and beneficial ownership narrative, professional reference letters from a reputable overseas bank or accounting firm, and a board resolution demonstrating the commercial rationale of the rail transit EPC project.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared capital injection purpose and actual infrastructure EPC disbursement profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized EPC master contract, the government concession or procurement award letter, the statutory construction and urban rail transit operating license, a certified project cash-flow budget, a SAFE-registered capital verification report by a licensed Chinese accounting firm, and detailed usage projections for every capitalized tranche.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of wealth for a shareholder contribution exceeding expected personal or corporate income levels
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of overseas shareholder bank statements, audited financial statements of the investing entity, board minutes approving the equity subscription, bank confirmation letters for any loans used to fund the injection, tax filing records, and a signed affidavit of source of wealth and source of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be wired from the foreign shareholder's own corporate bank account to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital account at a Tier-1 domestic bank using SWIFT MT103. The remittance purpose code must clearly identify a foreign direct investment equity injection into a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. On receipt, the bank verifies the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate and the underlying EPC business scope. Funds may be converted to RMB only for genuine business uses linked to the urban light rail project, including construction materials, labor, machinery, and subcontractor payments. If a capital verification report is required for statutory or local licensing purposes, a licensed Chinese accounting firm will issue a capital verification certificate after confirming the funds actually arrived in the capital account. Where the metro project requires a government bond escrow, the WFOE may transfer collateral or cash into an escrow account maintained with the designated bank under the project concession agreement, separate from the SAFE capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of EPC trade transactions will be executed through licensed clearing rails as follows: (1) direct supplier payments and subcontractor remittances via SWIFT MT103 with full supporting documentation; (2) import of rail signaling, catenary power equipment, and rolling stock components via Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) to mitigate transit risk; (3) Documentary Collections for low-risk, well-established suppliers; (4) RMB-denominated cross-border payments through CIPS for mainland and offshore project counterparties; and (5) government bond escrow settlements for performance guarantees and advance payment bonds, managed through the designated bank's escrow and guarantee services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD and RMB/EUR forward contracts with a licensed Chinese bank, limited to real transaction exposure arising from EPC contract receipts and supplier payments
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term project financing debt, subject to SAFE/PBOC approval and genuine underlying loan or bond exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available only to the overseas parent or offshore treasury counterpart, not directly executable in the onshore SAFE-regulated market
FX options may be permitted onshore for hedging trade and capital account transaction exposure, provided the bank transaction background documentation confirms the underlying cash flow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of each year covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in inclusion on the 'List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations'; after three consecutive years without correction, inclusion on the 'List of Seriously Illegal Enterprises' and the legal representative or responsible officer is banned from serving as legal representative or director for three years; market regulatory authority may impose an administrative fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 300,000 and in extreme cases revoke the enterprise registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the tax year; extension only with prior tax authority approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax from the statutory due date; administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid or mis-declared amount depending on the degree of fault; downgraded taxpayer credit rating; invoice controls and tax-exit denial; registration may be initiated for compulsory deregistration if the entity remains non-operational or fails to comply after repeated orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, jointly shared with Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of each year covering the preceding calendar year; changes to foreign-investment information must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing or material misrepresentation exposes the WFOE to a compliance reminder and correction order, inclusion in the dishonest or abnormal-operation list, revocation of preferential policy eligibility, restrictions on subsequent change-of-registration filings, and fines imposed under the Foreign Investment Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' Approval of Audited Annual Financial Statements and Profit-Distribution Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public authority filing; signed minutes and certified audit report kept at registered office and produced to SAMR, STA or company creditors upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts and audit report must be prepared and approved by the board of directors and shareholders within six months of the fiscal year-end, i.e. by 30 June of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare true and lawful financial statements violates the PRC Accounting Law; the company may be fined not less than RMB 10,000 and up to RMB 500,000, while responsible directors and financial officers may be fined RMB 5,000 to RMB 100,000; false accounts or concealment may lead to serious-illegal-list designation, license suspension, and criminal liability for fraud.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified Chinese CPA audit is legally required for the WFOE if any one of the following quantitative benchmarks is met in the fiscal year: (i) balance-sheet total assets exceed RMB 50 million at year-end; (ii) annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 80 million; (iii) average annual headcount exceeds 300 employees. A rail-transit EPC company (ISIC 4210) is also treated as an audit-mandatory enterprise because annual engineering revenue above RMB 50 million, or any single project contract value above RMB 100 million, must be substantiated by audited financial statements in the annual construction qualification review. In all cases where the enterprise files the Foreign Investment Information Annual Report, the financial data must reconcile to certified CPA financial statements; otherwise the annual report is deemed false and non-compliant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE), which are substantially converged with IFRS; small-scale enterprises are permitted to apply the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises only below the thresholds, but a licensed urban-light-rail EPC contractor is expected to apply full ASBE, including revenue recognition for long-term construction contracts and IFRS-compatible consolidation principles if the WFOE is a group entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities, the WFOE must submit beneficial-owner information to SAMR within 30 days of incorporation or any change and must reconfirm it annually through the Enterprise Annual Report window from 1 January to 30 June. Any share transfer or indirect ownership change that gives a natural person or controller ownership or voting power of 25% or more (or actual control through other arrangements) must be reported to SAMR within 30 days, and the on-site statutory Register of Members must be updated within the same 30-day reporting window. A transfer not reflected in the statutory register and in the SAMR filing cannot be invoked against bona fide third parties and may be administratively fined.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) with Name, Address, Capital Contribution and Transfer History
Register of Directors, Supervisor and Senior Management Officers
Register of Charges, Pledges and Security over Equity / Assets
Minute Book and Resolution Book of Shareholder Meetings and Board Meetings
Accounting Ledger and Voucher Register required by PRC Accounting Law

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,000 per year for registered-address agency or corporate-secretarial service in provincial capitals, excluding physical office lease; Tier-1 city full-service agent range is USD 1,500 - 4,000 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 20,000 per year depending on total assets, revenue complexity, group consolidation and the number of EPC project sites

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China's standard Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rate is 25%. A reduced 15% rate applies to certified High/New Technology Enterprises. Qualifying R&D expenditure is entitled to an additional 100% super deduction. A '3-year exemption and 3-year 50% reduction' CIT holiday may apply to qualifying public infrastructure project income, including certain rail transit construction projects. There is no general free-zone or patent-box CIT exemption; regional preferential regimes such as the Western Region encouraged-industry 15% rate may be available. Ordinary loss carryforward is 5 years, extended to 10 years for eligible High/New Technology Enterprises and certain small low-profit enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A Class) Form A100000 and supporting schedules, together with the Quarterly Provisional CIT Return Form A200000, filed through the State Taxation Administration's electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax system) for the registered WFOE.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. The annual CIT settlement return and the final CIT payment for the prior fiscal year are due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, including construction contract revenue, service revenue, engineering procurement and construction management revenue, net of value-added tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an ISIC 4210 urban light rail transit EPC WFOE, recognize contract revenue using the percentage-of-completion method where the contract outcome can be reliably estimated. Report all progress billings, design and supervision fees, equipment procurement income, and subcontract management fees. Do not net related-party cost reimbursements unless the WFOE is acting as a disclosed agent. Cross-border project services delivered by a non-resident contractor may create China-source service income subject to withholding; clearly track and disclose such amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to revenue: construction materials, direct labor, subcontractor costs, equipment leasing, utilities, and project overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs supported by valid tax invoices, contracts, customs declarations, bank payment records, or qualifying statutory vouchers. Related-party costs paid to overseas affiliates must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if the thresholds are met. Payments to non-resident subcontractors or service providers without proper withholding tax assessment and declaration may be disallowed and can trigger penalty liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible turnover-related taxes and surcharges: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharge, stamp duty, property tax, land use tax, and other taxes (excluding VAT and CIT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim foreign income taxes here; foreign income taxes are claimed as foreign tax credits in the CIT computation. If the WFOE contractually bears Chinese taxes of a non-resident subcontractor, such borne taxes may be capitalized into project costs only if supported by tax payment vouchers and correctly declared in the non-resident withholding filing. Surcharges and taxes already borne by the WFOE must be separately identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bidding costs, sales and marketing expenditures, business entertainment, travel expenses, project tender guarantee fees, and after-sales service costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Business entertainment expenditure is deductible only to the extent of the lower of 60% of actual expenditure and 0.5% of annual revenue. Commissions and agency fees paid to non-resident intermediaries require a commercial agreement, proof of services received, and, where China-source, withholding tax and treaty analysis. If a commission is paid to a related party, transfer pricing documentation and a benefits-received analysis are mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management and administrative staff costs, office expenses, professional fees, R&D expenses, employee welfare, labor union funds, and education funds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office management fees allocated by a foreign parent company to the Chinese WFOE are generally not deductible under Chinese domestic CIT rules. R&D expenditure can attract a 100% additional deduction if the project meets the statutory R&D definition. Payments to a non-resident parent for group management services must pass the 'benefit test' and cannot duplicate services already performed by WFOE employees. Treaty relief on any service fees requires evidence of beneficial ownership and no permanent establishment in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expenses, exchange differences, bank charges, and financing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related parties is China-source and generally subject to 10% withholding tax unless a treaty reduces the rate. The deductible interest amount is restricted by the thin capitalization debt-to-equity ratio: 2:1 for non-financial enterprises. If the WFOE is excessively leveraged by related-party loans, the excess interest will be recharacterized as a dividend and nondeductible. Interest must also be benchmarked under the arm's-length principle; absence of proper documentation invites transfer pricing audit adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net adjustments to accounting profit to compute taxable income: nondeductible penalties and fines, transfer pricing adjustments, timing differences, loss recapture, and expense cap reversals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any upward transfer pricing adjustment must be reported as an addition to taxable income. Withholding taxes on dividends are not deductible and must not appear here. Losses carried forward from prior years are limited to 5 years for ordinary enterprises, with a 10-year extension for High/New Technology Enterprises. All intercompany adjustments must be consistent with the contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and the arm's-length result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Tax Computation (Lines 20-34) - Tax Rate, Tax Credits, and Prior-Year Losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory 25% tax rate, preferential rates, tax holidays, foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and any deductible carryforward loss to compute the final assessed CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is a High/New Technology Enterprise, apply 15%. Claim foreign tax credits only for eligible foreign-source taxes on foreign-source income. Public infrastructure project income may qualify for the '3+3' tax holiday if the project is listed and approved. DTA relief for non-resident shareholders is not claimed in this section; it is applied by the withholding agent at the time of dividend distribution or refund application under the relevant tax treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return is punishable under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL) by a fine of up to CNY 2,000, or CNY 2,000-10,000 for serious non-compliance. Late payment attracts a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax under TCAL Article 32. Underreporting income or falsely declaring expenses constitutes tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, requiring restitution of the underpaid tax plus a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded. Criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law may lead to imprisonment of up to 3 years for relatively large amounts, or 3-7 years where the amount evaded is huge and exceeds 30% of the tax payable; fraudulent issuance or use of false VAT invoices may additionally trigger Criminal Law Article 205, with penalties up to life imprisonment in extreme cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For outbound dividend distributions by the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder, the WFOE as withholding agent must withhold 10% CIT unless a Double Tax Agreement (DTA) provides a lower rate. To invoke DTA relief, before or at the time of distribution, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's residence jurisdiction for the taxable year; (2) complete the non-resident taxpayer treaty benefit declaration and the Beneficial Owner Self-Declaration in the e-Tax system; (3) provide evidence of direct ownership of at least 25% of the voting capital if claiming the reduced 5% treaty dividend rate; (4) substantiate beneficial ownership and economic substance, demonstrating that the recipient is not a conduit or purely interposed company; and (5) ensure no permanent establishment in China to which the shares are effectively connected. If the full 10% has been withheld, the non-resident may apply for a refund of the over withheld tax within 3 years under TCAL Article 51.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: China-source royalties paid by the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise are subject to a statutory 10% WHT under EIT Law Article 3(3) and Article 37, plus VAT and surcharges where applicable. Cross-border interest paid by the WFOE to a non-resident lender or related party is also subject to a statutory 10% WHT. Under applicable DTAs, royalty and interest treaty rates vary, commonly 5%-10% for royalties and 0%-10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and TRC requirements. Excessive related-party interest may be recharacterized as a dividend under thin capitalization rules and then subject to dividend withholding treatment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million for annual related-party transfers of tangible property; RMB 100 million for related-party intangible property transfers; RMB 100 million for related-party financial asset transfers; RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions (including services). A Master File is required where aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. These thresholds trigger mandatory contemporaneous Local File and Master File preparation under SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under EIT Law Article 47, allowing recharacterization of arrangements that lack bona fide business purpose or economic substance. Under SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9, non-resident taxpayers claiming treaty benefits must satisfy the beneficial ownership test, which considers whether the entity has substantial business activities, employees, assets, and real decision-making authority. For the ISIC 4210 urban light rail transit EPC WFOE, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) — engineering, procurement, construction management, contract negotiation, risk assumption, invoicing, and project financing decisions — must actually be performed and managed in China with commensurate staff, premises, and risk. A letterbox or shell WFOE with no local substance cannot rely on treaty or transfer pricing benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE intentionally omits EPC progress billings from CIT revenue, uses forged or otherwise unlawful VAT invoices from shell subcontractors to inflate project costs, maintains a dual set of books, or underdeclares China-source revenue for a rail transit EPC contract. This conduct directly understates taxable income and evades Corporate Income Tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL), the tax authority recovers the underpaid tax, imposes a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and levies a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal liability arises under Article 201 of the Criminal Law; fraudulent VAT invoicing can additionally invoke Criminal Law Article 205, which carries fines and imprisonment ranging from short-term detention to life imprisonment for particularly huge amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law principles where a director abuses the WFOE's limited liability personality. Directors who direct, approve, or conceal false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and interest; their personal bank accounts, cars, and real estate may be seized through asset restitution proceedings. As responsible persons of a tax-dishonest enterprise, they may be placed on the Joint Punishment for Tax Dishonesty blacklist, subject to exit bans (travel restrictions), restrictions on high consumption and high-speed rail / civil aviation travel, disqualification from serving as directors, and potential criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years, or 3-7 years where the amount evaded is huge and exceeds 30% of the tax payable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalization Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive management fees, intercompany royalties, or related-party interest to its non-resident parent or sister companies without arm's-length benchmarking, without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or with a contrived debt-to-equity structure. These payments artificially shift Chinese EPC profits offshore, erode the Chinese tax base, and violate the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Articles 41 and 46 and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42, the tax authority may make transfer pricing adjustments, disallow excessive related-party interest under the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio, recharacterize excessive debt as equity, and impose a daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge on the underpaid tax. If the pricing scheme is determined to be tax evasion, TCAL Article 63 applies, exposing the WFOE to a penalty of 50%-500% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length transactions without obtaining proper transfer pricing studies, board resolutions, or economic substance documentation may be personally ordered to compensate the company for the resulting tax penalties, statutory interest, and audit costs. If the intercompany arrangement is a sham used to evade Chinese tax, the directors and controlling shareholders can be held civilly liable under the corporate veil piercing doctrine, subjected to travel bans via the tax dishonesty blacklist, and prosecuted criminally under Criminal Law Article 201 for conspiring in tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Abuse Lacking Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is a paper-only entity with no physical office, no staff, no independent business records, and no substantive project decision-making, while all core income-generating activities for the urban light rail transit EPC — engineering, procurement, construction supervision, risk acceptance, and financing — are performed by overseas affiliates. The WFOE is used solely as a conduit to collect Chinese project revenue and then route profits abroad under claimed treaty or intercompany arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 47 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule), the State Taxation Administration may recharacterize the arrangement, deny the claimed treaty benefits, and impose an upward adjustment to taxable income. SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 requires denial of DTA benefits where the recipient lacks beneficial ownership and economic substance. The resulting underpayment attracts a 0.05% per-day late-payment surcharge and, if intentional, a penalty of 50%-500% of the tax underpaid under TCAL Article 63.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the WFOE is a sham or mere instrumentality, courts and tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors and parent shareholders jointly liable for unpaid corporate tax, fines, and creditor liabilities. Directors may be personally required to restore diverted assets, and may have personal assets frozen or forfeited through civil asset restitution. They may also be blacklisted as tax-dishonest persons, restricted from leaving China, and criminally prosecuted for tax evasion if they knowingly used the shell structure to defraud the Chinese tax authority, resulting in imprisonment of up to 7 years for the most aggravated cases.
